stem:
Pallavi is given the front view, the top view, and the side view of one solid, drawn as three mutually perpendicular projections.

Which claim correctly decides how to identify the solid?

options.text: Match the solid from the front view alone.
Use the front, top, and side views together; one projection alone is not enough.
Naming the solid first forces those three views to exist.
Also treat any single corner sketch as enough under the same three-view rule.

teacher.key_rationale: A single projection does not fix a unique solid, so the front, top, and side views must be used together. Front alone, reversing name and views, or stretching the rule to any corner sketch miss that hinge.
